items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 10, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I’m talking about Cole Porter, Rogers & Hart, Gershwin. Those were the major composers at that particular time. And we took those tunes and dressed them up

ctx.x: What would the song list have been like? And do you recall how much money you first made? Your first gig? Your first paying gig?

Oh this was amazing. Because back in those days they were dancing, social dancing. When you play for a dance, you know there’s social dancing, we played “Out of Nowhere,” we played “Caravan,” we would play, for instance we would play “How High the Moon” but then we discovered that Charlie Parker wrote a tune on “How High the Moon” and he called it “Ornithology.” So at the same time as I was playing these tunes I © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

would go home with this other group, you know we’d practice with this other group at school. Not go home, I’d go to school. And the other group was playing “Ornithology” and “Hot House” and “Donna Lee.” And I discovered that it was the same as those standards they was playing at the dances. So we would play these tunes but then I would play the bebop tunes and they would play the traditional Cole Porter, Rogers & Hart melody, and we would play the bebop tunes along with them. You know that’s how, we learned them…
